cluster_micro
cluster_meso
cluster_macro

p3_micro_household_degree → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag intra_scale More household-layer contacts increase the chance that an exposure transition has a recorded source within the persistent household-like layer.

p3_micro_household_degree → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion upward An agent with more household-layer contacts participates in more dyadic pairs that can receive secondary exposure; variation in household degree therefore changes how unevenly attributed secondary events are distributed across household dyads.

p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward Source-attributed household exposures add dyads to the ever-attacked set, increasing the fraction of household dyads with any attributed exposure.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion upward Repeated household-attributed exposures concentrate in a subset of dyads, increasing dispersion of cumulative attributed exposures across household dyads.

p3_micro_household_attributed_flag → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction upward Individual household-attributed exposure events convert previously unaffected household dyads into attacked dyads, raising the fraction of dyads with any attributed exposure.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag downward Dyad-level secondary activity increases the chance that an agent’s exposure in that dyad carries a resolvable source attribution.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward A household dyad with more attributed secondary exposures is a more active transmission pair, making household-attributed exposure more plausible for its members.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward When attributed secondary exposures are unevenly spread across household dyads, individuals in high-concentration dyads face stronger within-dyad exposure pressure, making a household-attributed exposure more likely for those agents.

p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction intra_scale Concentration of attributed exposures in few household dyads can reduce the fraction of dyads with any attributed exposure by leaving many dyads unaffected.

p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward As a larger fraction of household-layer dyads accumulates attributed exposure, household transmission becomes more saturated; an individual exposure is then more likely to be recorded in the household-attributed category rather than in other settings.

p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion intra_scale A higher fraction of dyads with attributed exposure can coincide with more uneven accumulation across dyads, raising dispersion of dyad counts.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward A higher population-level household share increases the chance that any individual new exposure is attributed to the household layer, because household transmission is a larger component of the force of infection.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count downward A larger household share of all exposures implies more transmission occurs within household dyads, raising the expected number of attributed secondary exposures per household dyad.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction downward As household-attributed transmission grows as a fraction of all exposures, a greater proportion of household dyads will accumulate at least one attributed exposure event.

p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction → p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini intra_scale A larger household share can concentrate secondary exposures in fewer household dyads, raising dyad-level attribution inequality.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag downward High concentration of dyad-level attribution can shift source-resolved exposure events toward a small set of agents, affecting individual attribution status.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p3_micro_household_attributed_flag downward When attributed household exposures are concentrated in few dyads, agents in those high-count dyads face a higher chance of household-attributed exposure.

p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini → p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction downward Greater concentration of attributed secondary events can leave many dyads with no attribution, plausibly lowering the fraction of household dyads ever attacked.

N16 | p3_micro_household_degree Agent degree in the persistent household layer Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: d_i,H(t) = number of distinct undirected contact pairs at step t in layer l_H incident to agent i; l_H is the layer value with the largest mean consecutive-step Jaccard overlap of its edge set over all observed steps in the run; undefined if agent i is not observed at step t. N17 | p3_micro_attributed_exposure_flag Agent source-attributed exposure indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: A_i(t) = 1 if X_i(t) = 1 and the matched exposure event has a non-null partner_id; undefined if X_i(t) = 0 or if the matched event has a null partner_id, since no source can be resolved. N18 | p3_micro_household_attributed_flag Agent household-attributed exposure indicator Scale: micro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: H_i(t) = 1 if A_i(t) = 1 and the layer recorded on that exposure event equals l_H; 0 if A_i(t) = 1 and the layer is non-null and different from l_H; undefined if A_i(t) is undefined. N19 | p3_meso_dyad_secondary_count Household dyad attributed secondary exposure count Scale: meso | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: N_uv(t) = number of exposure events at step t with non-null partner_id whose unordered endpoint pair equals {u,v}, restricted to dyads {u,v} recorded as edges in layer l_H at step t; 0 for a listed dyad with no such event. N20 | p3_meso_dyad_secondary_dispersion Dispersion of attributed exposures across household dyads Scale: meso | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: CV(t) = SD_dyad(C_uv(t)) / mean_dyad(C_uv(t)), where C_uv(t) is the cumulative count of source-attributed exposure events in dyad {u,v} over observed steps up to t, taken over dyads recorded in layer l_H at any observed step up to t; undefined when fewer than two dyads or when the mean is 0. N21 | p3_meso_dyad_attack_fraction Fraction of household dyads with any attributed exposure Scale: meso | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: F(t) = count of dyads {u,v} recorded in l_H up to t with C_uv(t) >= 1 divided by count of dyads recorded in l_H up to t; undefined when the denominator is 0. N22 | p3_macro_household_attributed_fraction Household share of all observed exposure transitions Scale: macro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: f(t) = (sum over agents i of H_i(t)) / (sum over agents i of X_i(t)); undefined when the denominator is 0. N23 | p3_macro_dyad_attribution_gini Gini concentration of household dyad attributed exposures Scale: macro | Phenomenon: household_secondary_attack_concentration Definition: G(t) = (sum over dyads j of sum over dyads k of |C_j(t) - C_k(t)|) / (2 * n(t)^2 * mean_dyad(C(t))), where C_j(t) are cumulative dyad counts over dyads recorded up to t and n(t) is the number of such dyads; undefined when n(t) < 2 or the mean is 0.
